findings.body: Merely requesting the URL changes the user's topic notification preference without confirmation or CSRF protection; HEAD requests and link scanners can also invoke Rails GET routes and cause the same mutation.
findings.failure_mode: A read-like navigation unexpectedly mutates persistent user settings and is vulnerable to cross-site request forgery and prefetch side effects.
findings.impact: Merely requesting the URL changes the user's topic notification preference without confirmation or CSRF protection; HEAD requests and link scanners can also invoke Rails GET routes and cause the same mutation.
findings.root_cause: The patch maps an action that writes to TopicUser to the safe/idempotent GET verb.
findings.suggested_fix: Make GET render a confirmation page without changing state, and perform the preference update through a CSRF-protected POST/PUT endpoint. Change both unsubscribe route variants consistently.
findings.title: State-changing unsubscribe action is exposed through GET
findings.trigger: An authenticated user follows a forged top-level link, loads an attacker-controlled page that issues this request in a browser that sends cookies, or an authenticated mail/browser client prefetches the email link.
findings.verifier_reason: Patch adds GET route at line 440 mapping to topics#unsubscribe which mutates TopicUser.notification_level. The action is listed in ensure_logged_in but GET routes are vulnerable to CSRF via link prefetch/scanners since Rails CSRF protection only applies to non-GET requests by default.

findings.body: Dereferencing `tu` or comparing a nil notification level raises an exception, returning a 500 response instead of applying the requested preference.
findings.failure_mode: Valid authenticated navigation reaches an unhandled nil dereference or comparison error.
findings.impact: Dereferencing `tu` or comparing a nil notification level raises an exception, returning a 500 response instead of applying the requested preference.
findings.root_cause: The action assumes both the TopicUser record and its notification_level are always present, although the route is available for any visible topic.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `find_or_initialize_by` with an explicit regular default before comparing, or avoid the comparison and call `TopicUser.change` directly with the final muted level so a missing row is created safely.
findings.title: Unsubscribe crashes when no TopicUser row or level exists
findings.trigger: A logged-in user opens an unsubscribe URL for a visible topic for which they have no TopicUser record, or a legacy TopicUser row has a NULL notification_level.
findings.verifier_reason: Line 105-107 shows find_by returning nil when no TopicUser exists, then line 107 calls tu.notification_level which raises NoMethodError on nil. No nil check exists before the comparison.

findings.body: The misspelled public property creates a brittle, non-discoverable interface and forces the template to repeat the same typo, increasing the likelihood of future lookup failures during refactoring.
findings.failure_mode: The new controller/template API deviates from its intended terminology and must preserve an accidental typo to function.
findings.impact: The misspelled public property creates a brittle, non-discoverable interface and forces the template to repeat the same typo, increasing the likelihood of future lookup failures during refactoring.
findings.root_cause: The identifier transposes letters in the word `Notifications`.
findings.suggested_fix: Rename the property to `stopNotificationsText` and update the matching template reference.
findings.title: Computed property name misspells notifications
findings.trigger: A maintainer, plugin, or test refers to the new controller property using the conventional spelling `stopNotificationsText`.
findings.verifier_reason: Line 5 shows stopNotificiationsText with transposed letters (Notificiat instead of Notificat). This is a typo creating a non-standard API that must be matched exactly in templates.

raw_findings.body: The action changes the level only to regular, which remains eligible for reply, mention, quote, and private-message notifications. A tracking user can therefore continue receiving the same kind of email after using the link that promises to stop topic notifications.
raw_findings.failure_mode: The advertised unsubscribe operation completes successfully but does not honor the user's request for higher existing notification levels.
raw_findings.impact: The action changes the level only to regular, which remains eligible for reply, mention, quote, and private-message notifications. A tracking user can therefore continue receiving the same kind of email after using the link that promises to stop topic notifications.
raw_findings.root_cause: The transition treats regular as an unsubscribed state even though only muted suppresses all topic notifications.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Set the topic notification level to muted for every current level, or otherwise choose a target state that guarantees all notifications for the topic are suppressed.
raw_findings.title: Tracking and watching users are not actually unsubscribed
raw_findings.trigger: A user whose topic notification level is tracking or watching clicks the unsubscribe link, including a tracking user who received the email because of a mention or reply.

raw_findings.body: Dereferencing `tu` or comparing a nil notification level raises an exception, returning a 500 response instead of applying the requested preference.

raw_findings.body: The level is persisted while `notifications_reason_id` and `notifications_changed_at` retain their previous values, so later topic views can describe the new preference using an incorrect reason and downstream logic cannot identify it as an explicit user change.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Related fields in the persisted notification preference disagree after the update.
raw_findings.impact: The level is persisted while `notifications_reason_id` and `notifications_changed_at` retain their previous values, so later topic views can describe the new preference using an incorrect reason and downstream logic cannot identify it as an explicit user change.
raw_findings.root_cause: The new action bypasses the repository's centralized TopicUser notification-level update method.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Apply the new level through `TopicUser.change(current_user, params[:topic_id], notification_level: target_level)`, which records the user-change reason and timestamp consistently.
raw_findings.title: Direct save leaves notification-change metadata stale
raw_findings.trigger: A TopicUser whose current notification reason is created-topic, auto-watch, category-watch, or another non-user reason uses the unsubscribe link.

raw_findings.body: The other client receives no `/topic/:id` notification-level-change event and continues displaying the old topic notification state until it is manually reloaded.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Concurrent clients retain stale UI state after the server-side preference has changed.
raw_findings.impact: The other client receives no `/topic/:id` notification-level-change event and continues displaying the old topic notification state until it is manually reloaded.
raw_findings.root_cause: The patch writes the model directly instead of using the update path that publishes notification changes.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Use `TopicUser.change` for the update, or explicitly publish the same MessageBus notification-level-change event after a successful save.
raw_findings.title: Unsubscribe changes are not published to other open clients
raw_findings.trigger: The user has the topic open in another browser tab or session when they follow the email unsubscribe link.

raw_findings.body: The top-level `topicUnsubscribe` route resolves a top-level `topic-unsubscribe` template, while the patch adds only `templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs`; the intended confirmation and notification controls are therefore not rendered and the route may fail template lookup.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Ember cannot resolve the custom template associated with the entered route.
raw_findings.impact: The top-level `topicUnsubscribe` route resolves a top-level `topic-unsubscribe` template, while the patch adds only `templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs`; the intended confirmation and notification controls are therefore not rendered and the route may fail template lookup.
raw_findings.root_cause: The URL was declared as a top-level camel-cased route while its template was organized as a nested topic route.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Declare `this.route('unsubscribe')` inside the existing `topic` resource so the route name is `topic.unsubscribe`, or move the template to the top-level path expected by `topicUnsubscribe`. Keep the route, controller, view, and template naming consistent.
raw_findings.title: Route name does not match the added template path
raw_findings.trigger: The Ember application enters `/t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe` after the server-rendered email-link request or through a client-side transition.

raw_findings.body: The no-TopicUser exception, incorrect tracking/watching transition, redirect behavior, authorization, and request-method semantics can regress or remain broken without any automated failure.
raw_findings.failure_mode: The test suite does not exercise the feature's server-side contract or its failure branches.

raw_findings.suggested_fix: Add controller/request specs for unauthenticated access, inaccessible topics, canonical redirects, absent TopicUser rows, every notification level, idempotence, and a non-GET state-changing request protected by CSRF.

validated_findings.verifier_reason: Same root cause as candidate 3 - bypassing TopicUser.change also skips the MessageBus.publish at line 113 of topic_user.rb. Both are consequences of direct save vs using the change method.

validated_findings.body: The top-level `topicUnsubscribe` route resolves a top-level `topic-unsubscribe` template, while the patch adds only `templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs`; the intended confirmation and notification controls are therefore not rendered and the route may fail template lookup.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Ember cannot resolve the custom template associated with the entered route.
validated_findings.impact: The top-level `topicUnsubscribe` route resolves a top-level `topic-unsubscribe` template, while the patch adds only `templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs`; the intended confirmation and notification controls are therefore not rendered and the route may fail template lookup.
validated_findings.root_cause: The URL was declared as a top-level camel-cased route while its template was organized as a nested topic route.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Declare `this.route('unsubscribe')` inside the existing `topic` resource so the route name is `topic.unsubscribe`, or move the template to the top-level path expected by `topicUnsubscribe`. Keep the route, controller, view, and template naming consistent.
validated_findings.title: Route name does not match the added template path
validated_findings.trigger: The Ember application enters `/t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe` after the server-rendered email-link request or through a client-side transition.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 13 declares topicUnsubscribe as top-level route, but template is at templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs. Ember convention expects topic-unsubscribe.hbs at top level or unsubscribe nested under topic resource. Mismatch may cause template resolution failure.

validated_findings.body: The no-TopicUser exception, incorrect tracking/watching transition, redirect behavior, authorization, and request-method semantics can regress or remain broken without any automated failure.
validated_findings.failure_mode: The test suite does not exercise the feature's server-side contract or its failure branches.
validated_findings.impact: The no-TopicUser exception, incorrect tracking/watching transition, redirect behavior, authorization, and request-method semantics can regress or remain broken without any automated failure.
validated_findings.root_cause: The patch introduces a new persistent-state controller action and routes without adding any request-level tests for it.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Add controller/request specs for unauthenticated access, inaccessible topics, canonical redirects, absent TopicUser rows, every notification level, idempotence, and a non-GET state-changing request protected by CSRF.
validated_findings.title: New mutating endpoint has no controller/request coverage
validated_findings.trigger: CI runs after changes to authentication, routing, TopicUser creation, or notification-level transitions in this new action.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Test gap claims are stylistic/advisory. The patch does add unsubscribe to ensure_logged_in (line 28), and absence of tests is not a defect in the code itself.

validated_findings.body: This test still passes because it asserts only the preferences URL and List-Unsubscribe header, allowing the newly added per-topic link—the feature under review—to disappear unnoticed.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Automated coverage cannot distinguish a working per-topic unsubscribe email from one that only contains the pre-existing global preferences link.
validated_findings.impact: This test still passes because it asserts only the preferences URL and List-Unsubscribe header, allowing the newly added per-topic link—the feature under review—to disappear unnoticed.
validated_findings.root_cause: The test fixture was amended merely to satisfy the new interpolation argument without adding an assertion for the new behavior.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Assert that the generated message body contains the supplied `/t/1234/unsubscribe` URL, and add an HTML-mail assertion for the rendered topic link.
validated_findings.title: Updated email test never verifies the topic unsubscribe link
validated_findings.trigger: The locale interpolation, MessageBuilder body generation, or mailer option plumbing later stops including `unsubscribe_url` while the existing global preferences link remains present.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The test at line 172 adds unsubscribe_url parameter but this is test fixture setup, not a code defect. The claim about missing assertions is advisory/stylistic, not a bug in production code.

validated_findings.body: The misspelled public property creates a brittle, non-discoverable interface and forces the template to repeat the same typo, increasing the likelihood of future lookup failures during refactoring.
validated_findings.failure_mode: The new controller/template API deviates from its intended terminology and must preserve an accidental typo to function.
validated_findings.impact: The misspelled public property creates a brittle, non-discoverable interface and forces the template to repeat the same typo, increasing the likelihood of future lookup failures during refactoring.
validated_findings.root_cause: The identifier transposes letters in the word `Notifications`.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Rename the property to `stopNotificationsText` and update the matching template reference.
validated_findings.title: Computed property name misspells notifications
validated_findings.trigger: A maintainer, plugin, or test refers to the new controller property using the conventional spelling `stopNotificationsText`.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 5 shows stopNotificiationsText with transposed letters (Notificiat instead of Notificat). This is a typo creating a non-standard API that must be matched exactly in templates.
